item.title: VestGen secures growth capital from Willow Tree
item.description: Chicago-based VestGen Wealth Partners has secured growth capital from Willow Tree Credit Partners to support acquisitions and its advisor succession strategy. Willow Tree is a New York-based private credit firm that provides financing to middle-market businesses. Launched in late 2024 with 10 financial advisory firms collectively managing $5.3 billion in assets, VestGen added nine practices representing $2.2 billion in client assets in 2025.

item.title: Simplicity Group adds Denver RIA and Chicago tax shop in back-to-back deals
item.description: Simplicity Group bought two advisory firms on consecutive days this week, adding wealth management in Denver and a tax-led planning practice in Chicago. On Wednesday, Simplicity said it acquired Zen Wealth Management Group, a Chicago firm founded by Eddie Patel, who becomes a Simplicity partner. Key members of the MAIA team, including Scott Marek, Chandler te Velde and Desmond Dimond, will operate as Simplicity Wealth Advisors: Denver.

item.title: Adjuster Created Law Firm and Fake Claim to Defraud Insurer of $1M, Officials Charge
item.description: A former claims adjuster has been charged with defrauding the Pennsylvania insurer he worked for by taking payment of nearly $1 million for an accident claim under the guise that he was with a law firm representing the claimant. According to investigators, Johnson, while employed at Donegal in 2024 and 2025, created and opened Elite Injury Representatives, which appeared to be a law firm, and utilized his position as a claims adjuster to input fraudulent documentation into the Donegal claims file. Investigators maintain that Johnson, of Indiana, was employed as a claims adjuster by Donegal Insurance when he steered payment of $949,639 from Donegal to Elite Injury Representatives.

item.title: Tesla Launches Roadster at SpaceX Site in Latest Merger Hint
item.description: Gene Munster, managing partner of Deepwater Asset Management, said in a social-media post after the Roadster reveal that it “was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers.” His other major takeaway: Musk “can’t wait” to bring Tesla and SpaceX together. The electric vehicle performed a series of aerial stunts for a crowd of onlookers and Elon Musk, the chief executive officer of both Tesla and SpaceX, who called it “something that you haven’t seen in any movie.” “We need an audience to prove that it’s not AI or SI,” Musk said on stage at the livestreamed event, held at SpaceX’s 4,000-acre rocket development facility in McGregor, Texas. finally rolled out its long-delayed Roadster sports car — or rather, launched the vehicle into the sky.

item.title: Unbuckled Motorists Account for 28% of Traffic Fatalities: AAA
item.description: New research reveals that unbelted occupants account for a significant number of traffic deaths, according to the AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety (AAAFTS). drivers and passengers (28%) involved in a fatal crash in the last 30 days were unbuckled, pointing to a critical gap in seat belt use. The general trend is that older motorists and children tend to use seat belts more often than young adult motorists.

item.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Spending Contracts For Latest AI-Driven Startup Batch
item.description: This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here . Startup investors aren’t exactly hitting pause, but they did scale back on giant rounds this past week, with just two startup financings in the multiple hundreds of millions.

item.title: Lloyd’s issues guidance and expectations for broker-originated reinsurance structures
item.description: As industry focus grows on designing efficient structures to enable capital to connect with reinsurance risk, Lloyd’s has issued guidance on its expectations for any broker-originated reinsurance structures, which is a strategy that Lloyd’s itself believes is likely to see increasing demand. Lloyd’s framework for broker-originated reinsurance structures provides market guidance as to the approach, its expectations and what the approval requirements will be for broker-originated reinsurance structures. “Consistent with Lloyd’s broader approach, broker-originated reinsurance structures are subject to the standard new entrant approval process and ongoing oversight arrangements.”

item.title: Generali launching Lloyd’s Syndicate 2031 Red Bridge, to enhance access to reinsurance capital
item.description: The insurer said this move is “a significant step forward in the Group’s reinsurance strategy, enhancing access to diversified sources of risk capital while reinforcing long-term partnerships across the global reinsurance market.” Syndicate 2031 Red Bridge will assume a share of Generali’s outward reinsurance placements, across multiple lines of business. Global re/insurer Generali is the latest to enter the Lloyd’s market with what seems a sidecar-like syndicate as a way to enhance and make its reinsurance arrangements more efficient, while the announcements points to the potential for alternative and capital markets to be involved. Franco Urlini, Group P&C & Reinsurance Officer of Generali, explained, “The launch of Syndicate 2031 Red Bridge marks an important milestone in the evolution of our reinsurance strategy under the “Lifetime Partner 27: Driving Excellence” plan, with the goal to optimise capital at Group level.

item.title: APAC re/insurance markets face shifting risks and growth pressures: Gallagher Re
item.description: Roshan Perera, CEO of APAC at Gallagher Re, a global reinsurance broker and risk advisory firm, has outlined the key challenges and opportunities facing Asia-Pacific’s insurance and reinsurance markets in the company’s forthcoming APAC Market Watch report 2026 , examining slower premium growth, emerging risks and the strategic opportunities created by changing reinsurance market conditions. Non-life premium growth across the 14 major APAC markets covered by Gallagher Re reached 5% in 2025, although underwriting performance improved in many markets. Perera’s analysis will feature in Gallagher Re’s APAC Market Watch report 2026, scheduled for publication later this month, which will examine market developments across 14 individual APAC markets.

item.title: Ohio AG Sues Home-Improvement Companies for Allegedly Scamming Customers
item.description: Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson this week filed separate lawsuits against two home-improvement companies that allegedly took down payments from consumers but failed to provide the services promised or performed subpar work. One lawsuit seeks to help nine consumers who reported paying a combined $140,000 to Journey Home Restoration in Lorain County; the other involves five consumers who reported more than $60,000 in combined losses to The Metal Roof Company in central Ohio. The state’s lawsuit against Journey Home Restoration and its owner, Jason Kaczur, alleges that the company accepted the $140,000 from the nine customers for roofing, siding and gutter projects that were not completed.

item.title: NTSB Investigating Plane Crash in Wisconsin That Killed 6
item.description: Six people, including one child, died Tuesday night in a plane crash in Wisconsin after the pilot reported that ice was building up on the wings as he flew through a thunderstorm, according to authorities. The NTSB will lead the investigation into the crash, which happened about 10 miles (16 kilometers) west of Wisconsin Dells. Air traffic control approved the descent, and the plane began a right descending turn that increased in rate until communications and data tracking were lost, the NTSB said.

item.title: TDI Unveils Transparency Tool Showing Why Auto Policies are Declined
item.description: The Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) has introduced a tool that gives drivers insight into why personal auto insurance policies in their area were declined, canceled, or not renewed. The tool stems from House Bill 2067, passed in 2025, which requires insurance companies to report this information to TDI and provide written explanations when they decline, cancel, or don’t renew a home or auto insurance policy. The page also shows the number of cars with insurance policies and the counts of nonrenewals, cancellations, and declinations reported by insurance companies.

item.title: Founder Shield rebrands as The Baldwin Group
item.description: Founder Shield is adopting The Baldwin Group brand and becoming its Innovation Practice, five years after joining the insurance brokerage in 2021. Client portals, resources, and insights will remain available through foundershield.com and baldwin.com. The New York-based business provides insurance and risk management services to high-growth companies across life sciences, technology, media, financial services, and small business.

item.title: Fruga raises £1 million
item.description: Manchester-based insurance technology startup Fruga has raised £1 million from NPIF II–PXN Equity Finance, managed by PXN Ventures, and UK venture capital firm Haatch. Fruga provides technology that insurers, MGAs, and brokers can embed in their customer portals, allowing policyholders to earn retailer-funded credits on everyday spending toward their insurance renewal. Fruga also uses consented transaction data to help insurance providers identify changing customer needs and cross-selling opportunities.

item.title: GEICO expands pet insurance partners
item.description: The MetLife offering raises questions about GEICO’s relationship with Embrace, but comes as little surprise given GEICO’s recent switch in life insurance partners. GEICO Insurance Agency has long routed pet insurance leads to Embrace Pet Insurance Agency. Based on our testing across different ZIP codes, GEICO continues to route pet insurance leads to Embrace but also directs customers to MetLife and Liberty Mutual.

item.title: LigoPay prepara su expansión a seis mercados de LatAm y evalúa incorporar stablecoins
item.description: En paralelo, el negocio evalúa incorporar stablecoins para facilitar el movimiento transfronterizo de dinero, además de capitalizar su ventaja participativa en el sistema Tapp del Banco Central de Perú, donde participa junto a otros actores en la primera posición para el piloto que arranca este año. La empresa emisora de dinero electrónico LigoPay prepara una nueva etapa de crecimiento, esta vez fuera de Perú. La fintech ingresará a los mercados de Argentina y Bolivia este año y contempla expandirse a Colombia, Brasil, México y Ecuador para el 2027, con una estrategia centrada en la infraestructura de pagos y la integración con los sistemas locales.

item.title: Buenas Fuentes: Transbank atrae nueva ronda de compra, BBVA va por la oferta de banca patrimonial
item.description: Transbank atrae a cuatro bancos en una nueva ronda para cambiar de dueño en Chile Banco de Chile, Bci, Scotiabank y Banco Falabella figuran entre los interesados que podrían presentar ofertas no vinculantes por Transbank durante la tercera semana de octubre, en el nuevo proceso de venta de la principal red de adquirencia de Chile. item.title: Burned by Fire, Malibu’s Million-Dollar Mansions Face a New Threat: El Niño
item.description: But almost two years after the Palisades Fire destroyed approximately 700 homes in the city, properties are sitting empty and burned lots are struggling to find buyers. In Malibu, where multimillion-dollar homes have long commanded a premium precisely because they sit steps from the ocean, that proximity is increasingly becoming part of the risk residents are pricing in. High surf and erosion last month opened a massive sinkhole at a $10 million beachfront Malibu house tied to actor Nicolas Cage, rupturing a gas line, compromising the neighborhood’s only access road and prompting evacuation orders for 31 properties.

item.title: Teen’s Death Prompts Plan to Ban New York Central Park’s Horse-drawn Carriages
item.description: New York City lawmakers plan to ban horse-drawn carriages from Central Park, ending their more than 150-year run as an iconic, old-timey tourist attraction, following decades of opposition from animal welfare activists and the death of a teenage tourist last spring. Horse-drawn carriages have long been part of New York City’s history, but in an increasingly busy Central Park, this tradition has become a growing public safety liability,” Menin said in a statement. His death, which appeared to be the first fatality in a horse carriage accident since they were introduced in Central Park, reignited the debate over whether carriages, a romantic throwback to the city’s past, have a place in a modern metropolis.

item.title: EL Nino Expected to Drive Warmer Temps North While South, East Will See Wetter Conditions
item.description: El Nino will drive warmer and wetter conditions in the U.S., according to NOAA’s latest U.S. will see warmer-than-average temperatures, while wetter-than-average conditions are likely across the southern U.S., from California to Florida, and along the Eastern Seaboard. Drought conditions are expected to improve or end in the Southwest, Southern Great Plains, Southeast and parts of the East Coast, the report stated, while drought conditions are expected to develop or worsen across parts of the northern Rockies, along with northeastern Oregon and eastern Washington.

item.title: Asia’s Startup Funding At Near Record High In Q3, Driven By AI
item.description: Asia’s startup funding held up at the second-highest level in years in the third quarter, even as investment fell slightly from Q2 totals. Total funding is down substantially from the prior quarter, which was boosted by a $7.4 billion financing for China’s DeepSeek , but still the second-highest tally on record. Per Crunchbase data, roughly $27 billion — or 70% of all Asian startup funding in Q3 — went to China-based companies.

item.title: 777 co-founder Wander pleads guilty to $500m+ scheme to defraud lenders and investors
item.description: Josh Wander, one of the co-founders of investment firm 777 Partners, has pled guilty to wire fraud and securities fraud in connection with a $500 million plus scheme to defraud lenders and investors of the company. Whether perpetrated in the private or public markets, such brazen conduct undermines the integrity of our financial system and will not be tolerated.” The United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York stated yesterday, “WANDER, the co-founder and former CEO of 777 Partners, a private investment firm, orchestrated a multi-year scheme to defraud 777 Partners’ lenders and investors of more than $500,000,000. As part of that plea, Wander has agreed to forfeit at least $500 million in proceeds from the illegal scheme, United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald announced.

item.title: SafePoint targets $250m Nature Coast Re 2026-2 cat bond, for broadest coverage yet
item.description: Both tranches of the Nature Coast Re 2026-2 cat bond issuance are designed to provide SafePoint and its reciprocal underwriting entities with a source of fully-collateralized reinsurance protection covering losses from named storms across the states of Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Texas. SafePoint Insurance Company is back in the catastrophe bond, with an initial target to secure $250 million of multi-year named storm reinsurance protection from capital market investors through a Nature Coast Re Ltd. In 2025 SafePoint sponsored two catastrophe bonds, securing $200 million of annual aggregate and industry-loss trigger based reinsurance from a Nature Coast Re 2025-1 deal in January and then in April adding $150 million of indemnity based reinsurance with a Nature Coast Re 2025-2 issuance.

item.title: Moody’s estimates insured losses from hurricane Isaias in $2.5bn to $4.5bn range
item.description: Cotality (formerly CoreLogic), estimated that insured losses from wind and storm surge from hurricane Isaias will be in the $2 billion to $3 billion range, while Gallagher Re said industry losses will fall in the lower end of the low to mid-single-digit billions of dollars range and AM Best said insured loss estimates are expected to be in the low single digit range in billions of dollars. Moody’s RMS Event Response has now provided an initial estimate of insurance industry losses from recent hurricane Isaias, placing them in a range between $2.5 billion and $4.5 billion. Moody’s estimate is one of the higher, but still all the estimates top-out at $4.5 billion in range terms, at which level hurricane Isaias is not expected to be a significant reinsurance event, aside from perhaps a few very low layers and any quota share reinsurance participations that are exposed.

item.title: Moody’s RMS says Hurricane Isaias insured losses could hit $4.5bn
item.description: Catastrophe risk modeller Moody’s RMS Event Response has estimated total US private market insured losses from Hurricane Isaias to range from $2.5 billion to $4.5 billion, with a best estimate of $3.5 billion. Moody’s said its recent estimate covers insured losses associated with wind, storm surge and precipitation-induced flooding. The figure includes wind and storm surge losses in parts of the Gulf Coast and southeastern US, based on analysis of Moody’s RMS Event Response ensemble footprints in Version 25 of Moody’s RMS North Atlantic Hurricane Models.

item.title: VisionFund, Global Parametrics to develop Amazon Basin parametric cover
item.description: VisionFund, the financial inclusion arm of World Vision, working with Global Parametrics and co-financed by the InsuResilience Solutions Fund, will design a two-peril parametric meso-insurance for World Vision offices in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, and Peru as part of the wider Amazon Basin Initiative. VisionFund will leverage its extensive experience to design the solution, starting in the last quarter of 2026, as the Amazon Basin model will also be a template for replication in Southeast Asia and Southern Africa initially. By providing a tool that brings institutional risk financing World Vision can implement its pre-planned disaster response activities faster.” The integrated approach builds on VisionFund’s experience in inclusive insurance, including over eight years of climate meso-insurance and World Vision’s extensive disaster preparedness and response experience in the Amazon Basin region and globally.

item.title: Generali advances reinsurance strategy with launch of Syndicate 2031 Red Bridge at Lloyd’s
item.description: It is an extension of our strategy aimed at maintaining broad and diversified access to reinsurance and alternative capital markets while adding a further tool to the Group’s risk transfer capabilities.” Dawn Miller, Chief Commercial Officer of Lloyd’s and CEO of Lloyd’s Americas, said: “Our ambition is to attract the leading global underwriters to Lloyd’s, so we are delighted to be welcoming Generali with the launch of Syndicate 2031 Red Bridge. Global insurer Generali has entered the Lloyd’s marketplace with the launch of Syndicate 2031 Red Bridge, which will assume a share of the carrier’s outward reinsurance placements, across multiple lines of business. Franco Urlini, Group P&C & Reinsurance Officer of Generali, commented: “The launch of Syndicate 2031 Red Bridge marks an important milestone in the evolution of our reinsurance strategy under the “Lifetime Partner 27: Driving Excellence” plan, with the goal to optimise capital at Group level.

item.title: Florida Wins Key Ruling Allowing it to Enforce Law on Social Media Use by Kids
item.description: The state of Florida won a key court decision this week that allows it to enforce a ban on social media accounts for kids under 14 and other restrictions. The law bans social media accounts for Florida children under 14 and requires parental consent for use by kids who are 14 or 15. Industry trade groups the Computer & Communications Industry Association and NetChoice sued Florida, arguing that the law violated the free-speech rights of social media providers and users.

item.title: West Virginia Fire Commission Says State Really Needs More Firefighters
item.description: Staffing at fire departments is the top issue cited in the newly released Fire Prevention and Control plan by the West Virginia Fire Commission. “The manpower needs relative to fire and other related hazard responses are critical to the safety of the citizens of West Virginia and those responding to these emergencies and hazards,” the plan states. But the plan has no description of how many vacancies state fire stations have or how many firefighters would be needed for stations to meet OSHA standards.

item.title: Travelers Insurance Reports Solid Underwriting, Record Investment Income for Q3
item.description: Travelers Insurance reported continued solid underwriting and historic investment income for the third quarter along with higher catastrophe losses. “It was another in a run of successful quarters, with very strong underwriting performance across all three segments and a record result from our investment portfolio,” commented Alan Schnitzer, chairman and chief executive officer. “Our strong underwriting and investment results through the first nine months of the year reflect the strength of our franchise.

item.title: Santalucía and Zurich sign ten-year distribution alliance
item.description: Santalucía and Zurich Insurance have signed a ten-year alliance in Spain covering auto, funeral, and pet insurance. Santalucía will market Zurich’s auto insurance under its own brand across all distribution channels, while Zurich will distribute Santalucía’s funeral and pet insurance products. The arrangement combines Zurich’s auto underwriting expertise with Santalucía’s distribution network and experience in family protection.

item.title: AlloBrain raises $7 million with participation
item.description: Paris-based customer service AI company AlloBrain has raised $7 million in a round led by Varsity, with participation from longtime client Groupama and angel investors. Founded in late 2020 as AlloReview, AlloBrain combines AI agents, real-time assistance for customer service representatives, interaction quality assessments, and customer feedback analysis. AlloBrain also says its commercial model ties payment to lower service costs and higher customer satisfaction, with no payment due if those results are not achieved; contractual terms were not disclosed.

item.title: Travelers on Muse: “It’s early days”
item.description: “The first thing I would say just broadly about Muse and AI assistance, it’s early days, right? Travelers is exploring the opportunities and threats posed by Muse and AI shopping assistants, but executives expect a measured pace of adoption and say the insurer’s investments in digital distribution have prepared it to respond. Speaking during Travelers’ third-quarter earnings call, Michael Klein, executive vice president and president of Personal Insurance, said Muse is currently focused mostly on personal insurance.

item.title: Volvo Cars Expands Automated Driving Partnership With Nvidia
item.description: Volvo Cars is expanding its partnership with Nvidia to develop a new generation of driver-assistance and automated-driving technology, the companies said on Thursday, as carmakers race to bring increasingly advanced hands-free driving features to market. (Reporting by Mannes; Editing by Susan Fenton and David Gregorio) Get the latest insurance news sent straight to your inbox.

item.title: Swiss Re: Non-Economic Factors Drive Half of UK Liability Claims Growth
item.description: Non-economic factors have accounted for roughly half of liability claims growth in the U.K. Liability Claims Growth Could Increase Without Balanced Reforms, shows non-economic factors added 5 to 6 percentage points to liability claims growth in 2024. Related: Business Interruption Claims Are Approaching $1M Average Non-economic drivers include changes in laws and legal procedures, litigation funding and claimant behavior.

item.title: Report: 1 in 4 Taxis, Rideshare Vehicles Have Unfixed Recalls
item.description: More than one-in-four taxi and rideshare vehicles had at least one unfixed recall, according to an analysis across 16 major U.S. In New York City, 38.6% of medallion cabs had an unfixed recall, while 37.5% of taxi and rideshare vehicles had an unfixed recall in Seattle followed by 30.2% in Memphis. Consumers can check vehicles for unfixed recalls at carfax.com/recall .

item.description: As these convictions formed the basis on which the FCA took its action, we have revoked the bans of Colin Bermingham, Philippe Moryoussef, Jonathan Mathew and Christian Bittar and removed the associated Final Notices from FCA channels. The FCA has reviewed its regulatory action against individuals whose convictions have recently been overturned by the Court of Appeal . The FCA will take no further action against these individuals in relation to this matter.

item.title: Nascent Re issues $36m across Plymouth / Warwick preferred share insurance-linked securities
item.description: a licensed reinsurance transformer owned and operated by Bermuda-based Nascent Group, has issued another $36 million of preferred share insurance-linked securities, across two series named Plymouth and Warwick. The first issuance of listed insurance-linked securities from Nascent Re emerged earlier this year in March 2026, with a €10 million tranche of OFS Re Series 2026-001 preferred shares issued . These are the fifth and sixth individual issuances of ILS securities from Nascent Re that we’ve reported on, with all six seen to-date being in preferred shares form, likely representing some kind of collateralized reinsurance or private ILS arrangement.

item.title: CCRIF to pay US $17.4m to Panama after M7.7 quake triggers parametric coverage
item.description: CCRIF SPC, the regional parametric risk pool for the Caribbean and Central America, is set to make a payout of US $17.4 million to the government of Panama after the recent magnitude 7.7 earthquake triggered its parametric disaster insurance protection under the facility. “Panama’s decision to secure its CCRIF earthquake coverage through the Fondo de Ahorro de Panamá is a strong example of how parametric insurance can work alongside national savings and stabilization mechanisms as part of a layered approach to financing disaster risk.” Panama has been a beneficiary of parametric disaster insurance protection through the CCRIF since 2018. The parametric insurance payout will be made within 14 days of the quake, as the CCRIF sticks to its rapid disbursement of funds promise.

item.title: ICW Group names Travis Noland to newly created reinsurance and risk management role
item.description: ICW Group Insurance Companies, a US insurance provider, has appointed Travis Noland as Head of Ceded Reinsurance and Enterprise Risk Management. His deep expertise, strategic perspective, and collaborative leadership style make him uniquely qualified to lead our ceded reinsurance and enterprise risk management functions as we position ICW Group for the future.” ICW Group also pointed to Noland’s contribution to the development of its underwriting operations and teams. Noland has been with ICW Group since 2004, holding positions across reinsurance, catastrophe management and property underwriting.

item.title: CCRIF to make $17.4m payment to Panama after M7.7 quake triggers parametric coverage
item.description: CCRIF SPC, the regional parametric risk pool for the Caribbean and Central America, has announced it is to make a payout of US$17.4 million to the Government of Panama following the magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck the country on October 9, 2026. “Panama’s decision to secure its CCRIF earthquake coverage through the Fondo de Ahorro de Panamá is a strong example of how parametric insurance can work alongside national savings and stabilization mechanisms as part of a layered approach to financing disaster risk.” Since joining CCRIF in 2018, Panama has received three payouts totalling US$29 million for Hurricane Eta (2020) and 2024 rain events. Using its SPHERA earthquake model, CCRIF estimated peak ground acceleration of up to 0.5 g in Panama, the only CCRIF member country to experience shaking above the model’s 0.03 g reporting threshold.

item.title: Aon promotes Chris Rafferty to Chief Integration Officer for IMO
item.description: Aon, the professional services firm specialising in risk, retirement and health solutions, has appointed Chris Rafferty as the new Chief Integration Officer for its Integration Management Office (IMO). Rafferty joined the group in 2007 as Chief Operating Officer, a role he held for nearly 15 years. After several rewarding years as Aon’s Chicago Market Leader, I have begun transitioning into a new role as Chief Integration Officer for Aon’s Integration Management Office (IMO).

item.title: Broad AI Exclusions in Insurance Policies Could Create Uncertainty, Marsh CEO Says
item.description: A broad-based AI exclusion in insurance policies could create “real confusion and uncertainty,” Marsh CEO John Doyle said, calling for a more nuanced approach to assessing risks as the technology becomes increasingly embedded in business operations. AI agents can behave unpredictably and act autonomously, sometimes using access and permissions granted to them, raising questions about whether losses such as business disruption are covered by policies. Exclusions are provisions in a policy that specify which risks, events or losses are not covered.

item.title: Cyber Rates Are Down, Risks Are Up but Small Businesses Slow to Adopt
item.description: Despite lower rates and growing risks, adoption remains low among small- and mid-sized businesses, with the market penetration for cyber insurance estimated at just 10% to 20%, according to Swiss Re. The commercial cyber insurance market is strong and growing, but small to midsize businesses may be falling behind as cybercriminals ramp up AI efforts. “Cyber insurance is an important part of a comprehensive risk management strategy, particularly for small and midsize businesses with fewer resources to recover from an attack,” Kevelighan said.

item.title: People Moves: OneShield Appoints Brown as Chief Insurance Officer
item.description: Insurance technology company OneShield, headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts, appointed Terry Brown as chief insurance officer. Brown brings decades of insurance experience across the agency, carrier, and software sides of the industry. In this newly created role, Brown will shape the company’s AI-native capabilities and bring them to market.

item.title: Prex Perú recibe permiso para ampliar sus operaciones como emisor de dinero electrónico
item.description: La filial peruana de Prex recibió la autorización de la Superintendencia de Bancos (SBS) para ampliar sus operaciones como emisor de dinero electrónico, un servicio adicional que complementará su actual licencia como empresa de crédito. El country manager para la región andina, Ignacio Nina, dijo a iupana , que esta expansión de sus servicios les permitirá explorar y desarrollar nuevos negocios para el próximo año. CCC Intelligent Solutions (Chicago) has agreed to be acquired by a private investment consortium led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $6.1 billion. “With GTCR and Elliott’s experience and resources, we will continue to build on our momentum and extend our leadership,” Ramamurthy comments. Mark Anderson, Managing Director and Head of Technology, Media & Telecommunications, GTCR.
